title: MOCK PAPER — General Studies Practice Test
subtitle: LeakTrace test series · Not a real examination · Time: 2 hours · Maximum marks: 100
instructions: All questions are compulsory. Answers must be written in the answer booklet provided by the centre.
Marks for each question are shown in brackets at the end of the question. Use of calculators is not permitted.
This paper is an invented practice paper written for research on document fingerprinting.
questions: Explain in your own words why the sky appears blue during the day but turns orange or red near sunrise and sunset. [3]
A train leaves a station at 9:15 and travels at an average speed of 72 kilometres per hour. How far will it have travelled by 11:45 on the same morning? [2]
Define the term photosynthesis and name the two raw materials that a green plant needs to carry it out successfully. [2]
Rewrite the following sentence in the passive voice: The committee approved the new library budget after a long discussion. [2]
Describe three ways in which a village panchayat contributes to local development and give one example of each. [6]
Find the value of x if three times the number, decreased by seven, is equal to twice the number increased by five. [3]
State Newton's second law of motion and calculate the force needed to accelerate a bicycle of mass twelve kilograms at two metres per second squared. [4]
Why is it important to conserve groundwater in regions that receive very little rainfall? Suggest two practical measures a community could adopt. [5]
Read the line carefully and identify the figure of speech used: The classroom was a beehive of activity before the final bell rang. [2]
Name the three states of matter and explain, with the help of a simple everyday example, how a substance can change from one state to another. [5]
The perimeter of a rectangular garden is eighty metres and its length is three times its breadth. Calculate the area of the garden. [4]
Distinguish between a fundamental right and a directive principle of state policy, mentioning one feature that is common to both. [4]
Write a short paragraph of about eighty words on the importance of reading newspapers regularly in the life of a student. [5]
What is meant by the term renewable energy? List four sources of renewable energy and state one advantage of each source you have listed. [6]
A shopkeeper buys a table for twelve hundred rupees and sells it at a profit of fifteen percent. Find the selling price of the table. [3]
Explain the role of the heart in the human circulatory system and describe the path that blood follows through its four chambers. [5]
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence and justify your choice: The athlete was (affected / effected) by the sudden change in weather. [2]
Describe the main causes of soil erosion and discuss how farmers can reduce the damage caused by heavy rain on sloping fields. [6]
Simplify the expression and write the answer in its lowest terms: three fourths plus five sixths minus one third of the total. [3]
Why do we observe seasons on the Earth? Draw a neat labelled diagram to support your explanation and mention the role of the tilted axis. [5]
Summarise in about sixty words the advantages and disadvantages of using mobile phones in school classrooms during lessons. [4]
List any four safety rules that must be followed while working in a school laboratory and explain why each rule matters. [4]
The ratio of boys to girls in a school is seven to five. If there are four hundred and eighty students altogether, find the number of girls. [3]
Explain how a democratic government differs from a monarchy, giving one advantage and one limitation of the democratic form of government. [4]
Convert the following direct speech into indirect speech: The teacher said to the students, "Submit your projects before the holidays begin." [2]
What is the difference between a conductor and an insulator? Give two examples of each and state one use of each example. [5]
Describe the importance of trade between countries and explain how a rise in the price of fuel may affect the cost of everyday goods. [5]
A water tank is shaped like a cylinder with a base radius of seven decimetres and a height of two metres. Calculate its capacity in litres. [4]
Write a formal letter to the principal of your school requesting permission to organise a book fair on the school premises next month. [6]
Explain the process of digestion in humans and name the organs through which food passes from the mouth to the large intestine. [5]
In what ways did the invention of the printing press change the spread of knowledge and ideas across different regions of the world? [5]
Calculate the simple interest earned on five thousand rupees invested at eight percent per annum for a period of three years. [3]
Write the antonyms of the following words and use any two of them in sentences of your own: generous, ancient, gradual, victory. [4]
Why are forests described as the lungs of the Earth? Discuss three consequences of large scale deforestation on the local climate. [5]
Differentiate between weather and climate, and explain why a single hot day cannot be taken as proof of a changing climate. [4]
The angles of a triangle are in the ratio two to three to four. Find the measure of each angle and classify the triangle. [4]
Explain the meaning of the proverb a stitch in time saves nine and describe a situation from daily life where it applies. [3]
Discuss the contribution of any one scientist from India whose work has influenced modern science, and mention one key achievement. [5]
How does a magnet attract objects made of iron? Describe a simple experiment to find the poles of a bar magnet using a thread. [4]
Write an essay of about one hundred words on the role of sports in building discipline, teamwork and confidence among young people. [6]
